sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Nijmegen is shrinking street parking in the walled centre by stages, and the plan has been softened more than once. Street parking inside the singels is paid Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 23:00, the first ring to 21:00 and wider zones to 18:00; the college decision of 19 May 2026 took effect on 1 June 2026 [0]. Under the 2026A decision, resident permits are capped at 90 percent of on-street spaces, with one permit per address in the Centrum zones and two in zones K and L; as a general rule no permits are granted for new-build [1].

The main question is zone B, the pedestrian area behind the road barriers. In September 2024 the city planned to end all street parking there from 15 September 2025 and move residents and businesses into four garages [2]. After a college decision of 17 December 2024 and a council motion of 19 February 2025, a revised June 2025 plan withdrew the street permits of the 39 businesses on 1 January 2026 and let residents keep existing street permits until 31 December 2032; abolition is a plan, and parts of the plan are worded as proposals in the document [3]. The city's page now states that since 1 January 2026 businesses park in the garages, residents who swap to a garage subscription get 50 percent off in 2026 or 25 percent in 2027, valid until 1 January 2036 [4]. A letter of 22 December 2025 said that a lottery for Plein 1944 subscriptions would be held in early January 2026; the outcome is not shown [5]. Three zero-emission zones cover business vans and lorries since 2025, with private cars not covered [17].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The 2024 development rules, which were due to be adopted on 19 November 2024, set 0.70 spaces per dwelling in the inner city, with a visitor norm of 0.00; the document does not confirm adoption [12]. The June 2025 plan expects about 250 residents to move their cars into the garages over the coming years and asks to study turning the Eiermarkt garage into a subscribers-only garage; reconstruction of Kelfkensbos, planned from September 2025, could leave Eiermarkt and Mariënburg reachable only via Hertogstraat [6]. The municipality has three P+R sites, Noord, Eerste Oude Heselaan and West, open 24 hours [14], and lists ten surface car parks in the centre [15]. Signs on the routes into the centre show free garage spaces, and the open-data portal offers real-time capacity and occupancy for six garages [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The six municipal garages in and around the centre charge 3.90 euros an hour from 08:00 to 18:00 and 0.50 euro in the evening, with a 24-hour maximum of 16 euros in three of them [7], up from 3.60 euros in 2024 and 2.80 euros in 2019 [8][9]. In 2020 the council said the centre's garages were full only at peak moments and events, positioning them as the high-priced park-and-walk option [11]. Radboud University moved its campus rates to 2.90 euros an hour from 1 April 2026, following the municipality's rates [10].

Our data cover three car parks with 964 spaces, measured for about eight weeks since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 36% on weekdays and 42% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The Eerste Oude Heselaan park-and-ride (264 spaces) is the fullest at 73% and 75% and reached 99% on a Saturday at noon. The Molenpoort roof (350) averaged 44% on weekdays and 58% at weekends. P+R Noord (350) averaged 1%, with one isolated full reading that looks like an anomaly. The centre garages are not in our feed. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
